newsitem.title: KENYA: Thin bank business in Kenya because of strike.
newsitem.headline: Thin bank business in Kenya because of strike.

text.p: Kenyan commercial banks slashed their opening hours to a minimum on Thursday because of a strike by bank staff to protest at the sacking of two colleagues.
Major banks in the capital Nairobi said senior management were working as cashiers and services were cut because of the strike. Some major commerical banks were open for as little as one hour.

Strike leaders said they were protesting at the sacking of two colleagues at two commercial banks. One of the two men was sacked because he had leaked details of his bank's staff salary plans for the next year, a commercial banker said.
Foreign exchange dealers said trading was thin because of the strike.
"We haven't done any business today because the back office, which is manned by unionised staff, are not paying out. We're just giving out levels," a dealer told Reuters.
"Those banks whose processing departments employ unionised staff are not trading," another dealer said.
